title: Generalized Swelling
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a child presenting with generalized edema (periorbital — worse in morning, then leg/scrotal), weight gain, frothy urine (proteinuria), and fatigue. Nephrotic syndrome: massive proteinuria (>3.5g/day or >40mg/m2/hr in children), hypoalbuminemia (<2.5), edema, hyperlipidemia. Most common cause in children: minimal change disease (MCD) — 80-90%. Often preceded by viral URI. Diagnosis: UA — 3-4+ protein, oval fat bodies. 24h urine protein confirms nephrotic range. Renal biopsy NOT routinely needed in children (MCD most common and responds to steroids). Treatment: prednisone 2mg/kg/day (response = remission in 2-4 weeks confirms MCD). Salt/fluid restriction. Diuretics for severe edema. If steroid-resistant or frequently relapsing: consider biopsy, alternative immunosuppression (cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine). Vaccinate before immunosuppression (pneumococcal). Monitor for complications: infection (loss of immunoglobulins), thrombosis (loss of antithrombin III).
chief_complaint: Generalized edema, frothy urine, weight gain
